Module std::vec

A contiguous growable array type with heap-allocated contents, written as Vec<T>.

Overview

Vectors have O(1) indexing, amortized O(1) push (to the end), and O(1) pop (from the end).

Examples

You can explicitly create a Vec with Vec::new:

let v: Vec<i32> = Vec::new();

Or you can use the vec! macro:

let v = vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5];

Capacity and Reallocation

The capacity of a vector is the amount of space allocated for any future elements that will be added onto the vector. This is not to be confused with the length of a vector, which specifies the number of actual elements within the vector.

Guarantees

Due to its incredibly fundamental nature, Vec makes a lot of guarantees about its design. This ensures that it's as low-overhead as possible in the general case, and can be correctly manipulated in primitive ways by unsafe code.
